nary_nodes.label: Ebola treatments trial begins
evidence: A trial of potential treatments for the species of virus behind the current deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has begun
The first patient has been enrolled in DR Congo

nary_nodes.label: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo
evidence: the current deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo
The current outbreak of Ebola in DR Congo began in May
A trial of potential treatments for the species of virus behind the current deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has begun

nary_nodes.label: Confirmed cases and deaths in DR Congo
evidence: More than 1,400 cases and 438 deaths have been confirmed in the country
there have been 1,460 confirmed cases in DR Congo, with 150 suspected cases and 452 deaths, as of 1July
More than 1,400 cases and 438 deaths have been confirmed in the country, according to the WHO.

nary_nodes.label: Recovered patients in DR Congo
evidence: According to the WHO, 213 people have recovered.

nary_nodes.label: Cases in Uganda and France
evidence: There have also been 20 confirmed cases in Uganda, leading to two deaths, and one confirmed case in France, as of 1 July.

nary_nodes.label: Case in Tshopo province
evidence: the body of a pregnant woman tested positive for Ebola in the neighbouring Tshopo province

nary_nodes.label: Case in Haut-Uele province
evidence: an individual suspected of having Ebola reportedly fled from an isolation unit in Ituri and later tested positive in the nearby Haut-Uele province

nary_nodes.label: Increase in testing laboratories
evidence: Previously, four laboratories were testing for Ebola, but that number has now increased to 10.

nary_nodes.label: WHO chief statement on treatments
evidence: Speaking to reporters from the WHO headquarters in Geneva on Thursday, Tedros said: "Even without approved therapeutics, people are recovering from this disease, but of course, we could save many more lives with safe and effective therapeutics in our toolkit."

nary_nodes.label: Health Minister statement on trial launch
evidence: DR Congo's Health Minister Dr Samuel Roger Kamba said the launch "represents a significant step forward, offering renewed hope to patients, their families, and affected communities".

nary_nodes.label: Outbreak restricted to eastern provinces
evidence: Congolese health authorities have said the outbreak is currently restricted to three eastern provinces - South Kivu, North Kivu and Ituri.

nary_nodes.label: News agencies report case in Tshopo
evidence: the Reuters and AFP news agencies report that the body of a pregnant woman tested positive for Ebola in the neighbouring Tshopo province

nary_nodes.label: Report of individual fleeing isolation
evidence: an individual suspected of having Ebola reportedly fled from an isolation unit in Ituri and later tested positive in the nearby Haut-Uele province
Additionally, an individual suspected of having Ebola reportedly fled from an isolation unit in Ituri and later tested positive in the nearby Haut-Uele province.

nary_nodes.label: Improved diagnosis across region
evidence: DR Congo's health ministry said it has improved diagnosis across the affected region.

nary_nodes.label: Potential to be one of largest outbreaks
evidence: According to both Africa CDC and US public health authorities, the current outbreak has the potential to be one of the largest ever, because it was spreading for weeks before it was confirmed to be Ebola.

nary_nodes.label: Conflict hinders outbreak response
evidence: International organisations also warn that conflict in eastern DR Congo is making it more difficult to tackle the outbreak.

nary_nodes.label: Public health emergency declared
evidence: The situation has been declared a public health emergency by the WHO

nary_nodes.label: Public gatherings banned
evidence: public gatherings were banned in both these provinces, along with neighbouring Bas-Uele and the capital, Kinshsasa
Earlier this week, public gatherings were banned in both these provinces, along with neighbouring Bas-Uele and the capital, Kinshsasa

nary_nodes.label: Contact-tracing efforts launched
evidence: Authorities are said to have launched contact-tracing efforts across Tshopo and Haut-Uele.

nary_nodes.label: Body transported to Kisangani
evidence: The woman reportedly died in Ituri, before her body was transported by motorbike to Tshopo's main city, Kisangani

nary_nodes.label: Individual fled isolation unit
evidence: an individual suspected of having Ebola reportedly fled from an isolation unit in Ituri
